name: GPU Direct Volume Rendering with Anisotropic Shading
definition: A ray-casting DVR algorithm on GPU that uses precomputed normals and covariance matrices to perform anisotropic shading using Ward or Lafortune BRDFs.
summary: GPU Direct Volume Rendering with Anisotropic Shading is a GPU-based ray casting algorithm that enhances visual quality by applying anisotropic shading models to volumetric data, distinguishing itself by precomputing covariance matrices to reconstruct local surface orientation and anisotropy axes on-the-fly.
